newsitem.title: ITALY: Albania force should withdraw if vote slips - Italy.
newsitem.headline: Albania force should withdraw if vote slips - Italy.

text.p: Italian Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta said on Wednesday that a multinational security force in Albania should be withdrawn if an agreement between political parties to hold elections by the end of June is broken.

"If this agreement fails, both the United Nations and the governments involved...should look again at the reasons for the mission and proceed with its withdrawal," Andreatta told the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) at a question time session.
Italy is leading the multinational force which began deploying on its three-month, U.N.-backed mission to oversee humanitarian aid deliveries last month.
Andreatta was asked whether tensions between Albanian President Sali Berisha and Bashkim Fino, the prime minister of an all-party government, were jeopardising the security mission.

Members of a delegation of European parliamentarians said in Tirana earlier this week that Albania would be thrown back into chaos if political parties failed to reach a compromise over arrangements for the general election.

Berisha is refusing to compromise on his demand that citizens' committees, set up in some towns as Albania slid into anarchy after the collapse of dubious savings schemes, must be disbanded before the vote. Albania's parliament must agree on electoral procedure for the vote to go ahead on June 29.
